video_title: OKC Gets One Back at Home, Knicks Up 2-0 on Josh Hart's RECORD Night: Can They Sweep The CAVS?!

quotes.speaker: Paul Pierce
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavs' strategy and chances after being down 2-0
quotes.excerpt: I actually like that game playing today to say, all right, we going to give the ball out of Brunson's hand.
quotes.quote: I actually like that game playing today to say, all right, we going to give the ball out of Brunson's hand. Let's see if Josh Hart can make some shots. But unfortunately, Josh Hart found his rhythm, ended up with a play-off career high. And then once they got discouraged from that, the defense was just inconsistent throughout the game, especially the third quarter. They couldn't score points, they couldn't get stops. Brunson was finding out open man being selfish and as a great player like Brunson, he did a magnificent job at facilitating as they got the ball out of his hands and the Nick just got hot from three points, they knocked down shots. I'm just not sure what adjustments, but I can't say this. The Cavs they went two straight seven game series. They were down 0-2 to Detroit. So, if they can extend the series, this is what I'm saying in the locker room if I'm in Cleveland. I'm like, look guys, we were already down 2-0. We've been in this place before. We can come out the number one seat. We can climb out of this. Obviously role players play better at home. Even your stars will be more comfortable at home. You'll have that crowd to get momentum when you make runs. So I'm not counting them out. I did that in Detroit with Detroit, but I'm not counting them out their veteran group and I think they'll find a way to get back in the series.

quotes.quote: I think they could play better. I mean ultimately came down to a show that just don't have enough depth to play against to beat the Knicks, right? Ultimately the difference was the shooting. The Knicks lived with some of those open looks from those guys, but they'll hit them more at home. They lost the game by 16 points. The difference on three point shooting was 12 points or they out shot them by four more threes. There's 12 points right there and they also missed 10 free throws. They make half their free throws, shoot a little better from three, it's a lot more competitive. They'll shoot better at home. But ultimately, they're going to need big nights outside of the guys. They only had one big night from Donovan Mitchell. It wasn't even a big night, it was like a decent night. They need more scoring. They got to find ways to score more and they're going to need like big nights from either Evan Mobley and Jarred Allen or James Harden and somebody else like Max Strus. They didn't have much bench production. They just need some scoring tonight. They just didn't shoot well. They missed a lot of free throws and the Knicks got to hand on the game. quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown's successful coaching and adjustments for the Knicks

quotes.quote: Mike is making the adjustments. You know what I'm saying? And this is this is why they brought him in. You know what I'm saying? quotes.speaker: Danny Green
quotes.summary_phrase: OKC's defensive strategy to be physical and mix up coverage against Wemby
quotes.excerpt: OKC mixed it up and they used Hartenstein finally, which I said they should.
quotes.quote: OKC mixed it up and they used Hartenstein finally, which I said they should. You can't just put one guy on, you can't give any superstar player a steady diet of the same thing. So they were physical with Wemby. They grabbed, they held. They're going to continue to do that. They're going to get away with some stuff, some stuff they're going to call. Hartenstein had eight offensive rebounds, four defensive. He was active. He was keeping them alive, getting them second possessions. Also setting that Gortat screen, you know, boxing Wemby out so he couldn't block shots, but SGA was a totally different player. He was aggressive, getting to his spots, beating the double team. I also don't understand why Daigneault, even though he made the right adjustments and won this game, why are you taking the superstars off the floor when Wemby goes off the floor? He changed that a little bit in game two though. He changed it throughout, but the start, when they first came out, all three of them were on the bench and I'm like, that's crazy. But their bench produced. They got lucky. Jared McCain, AJ Mitchell, Kason Wallace, like they had like a plus 10 on San Antonio's bench. So they but they won't do that on the road unless you give them a chance to have one of those guys on the floor. Like when Wemby's out, you don't sub SGA at the same time Wemby goes in and out. Like that doesn't make sense. You keep him in the game so he has an advantage to get to the rim, to get to those spots without a contest. Early on he did it. He changed it as it goes on, but I just couldn't I couldn't understand that why he was doing that. But they played a different game when it came to addressing Wemby and being physical with Hartenstein. They played him more minutes and also SGA being more aggressive, more efficient on the floor. He got some free throws a little more, but he got his 30 points. He has to have his 30 points for them to be competitive.
